outcome: Type of Fecal Incontinence (e.g., urge incontinence)
Etiological factors for Fecal Incontinence (e.g., anal fistula, history of anal surgeries, rectal tumors, pelvic radiotherapy, history of pelvic surgeries)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 200 men and 200 women diagnosed with Fecal Incontinence who underwent anatomical and physiological evaluation in a tertiary referral center specializing in pelvic floor disorders.
finding: Significantly different etiological factors and physiological characteristics for Fecal Incontinence were found in men compared to women, including variations in sphincter defects, anal pressures, rectal sensitivity, and anorectal dyssynergia.
cross-section timing: Data was collected during anatomical and physiological evaluation of patients presenting to a tertiary referral center.
